correctness.rationale: The rates exactly specialize arXiv:2611.09180v1 equations (5)-(7). In u=k*rho1, v=k*rho2 and c=k-b-log k, the exact logistic odds give a C2 limit F=(exp(-c+2u+v)-2u,u-v), whose saddle-node is at u=v=1/3, c=1+log(3/2). The O(1/k) expansion yields the -1/k fold shift. A full-simplex subsequential compactness argument forces any other equilibrium either to the unique hyperbolic uniform state or a vertex; near vertices it forces u,v to remain bounded and to satisfy the limiting root equation, proving the count. Exact Jacobian signs give stable nodes and saddles; the source linearization gives stable uniform state. The actual bundled checker verified representative finite-b folds and branches, with finite computation explicitly not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The defining new physical model has numerically observed saddle-node ordered phases whose location and global multiplicity at extreme drive are natural unanswered parameters. The theorem determines their full high-bias equilibrium phase boundary, the nontrivial logarithmic offset and next correction, all stable versus saddle types and minority-density asymptotics. It shows an exponentially large separation between the fold and known Hopf scales. It is a structural complete classification, not a cosmetic normalization, one-sample computation or routine re-evaluation of a known table.
